Updates `astral-sh/setup-uv` from 5 to 7
Release notes

Sourced from astral-sh/setup-uv's releases.

v7.2.1 🌈 update known checksums up to 0.9.28

Changes

🧰 Maintenance

  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.28 @github-actions[bot] (#744)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.27 @github-actions[bot] (#742)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.26 @github-actions[bot] (#734)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.25 @github-actions[bot] (#733)
  • chore: update known checksums for 0.9.24 @github-actions[bot] (#730)

📚 Documentation

  • Clarify impact of using actions/setup-python @​eifinger (#732)

⬆️ Dependency updates

  • Bump zizmorcore/zizmor-action from 0.3.0 to 0.4.1 @dependabot[bot] (#741)

v7.0.0 🌈 node24 and a lot of bugfixes

Changes

This release comes with a load of bug fixes and a speed up. Because of switching from node20 to node24 it is also a breaking change. If you are running on GitHub hosted runners this will just work, if you are using self-hosted runners make sure, that your runners are up to date. If you followed the normal installation instructions your self-hosted runner will keep itself updated.

This release also removes the deprecated input server-url which was used to download uv releases from a different server. The manifest-file input supersedes that functionality by adding a flexible way to define available versions and where they should be downloaded from.

Fixes

  • The action now respects when the environment variable UV_CACHE_DIR is already set and does not overwrite it. It now also finds cache-dir settings in config files if you set them.
  • Some users encountered problems that cache pruning took forever because they had some uv processes running in the background. Starting with uv version 0.8.24 this action uses uv cache prune --ci --force to ignore the running processes
  • If you just want to install uv but not have it available in path, this action now respects UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH
  • Some other actions also set the env var UV_CACHE_DIR. This action can now deal with that but as this could lead to unwanted behavior in some edgecases a warning is now displayed.

Improvements

If you are using minimum version specifiers for the version of uv to install for example

[tool.uv]
required-version = ">=0.8.17"

This action now detects that and directly uses the latest version. Previously it would download all available releases from the uv repo to determine the highest matching candidate for the version specifier, which took much more time.

If you are using other specifiers like 0.8.x this action still needs to download all available releases because the specifier defines an upper bound (not 0.9.0 or later) and "latest" would possibly not satisfy that.

🚨 Breaking changes

Updates `actions/upload-artifact` from 4 to 7
Release notes

Sourced from actions/upload-artifact's releases.

v7.0.0

v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Add proxy integration test by @​Link- in actions/upload-artifact#754
  • Upgrade the module to ESM and bump dependencies by @​danwkennedy in actions/upload-artifact#762
  • Support direct file uploads by @​danwkennedy in actions/upload-artifact#764

New Contributors

  • @​Link- made their first contribution in actions/upload-artifact#754

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/compare/v6...v7.0.0

v6.0.0

v6 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/upload-artifact@v6 now runs on Node.js 24 (runs.using: node24) and requires a minimum Actions Runner version of 2.327.1. If you are using self-hosted runners, ensure they are updated before upgrading.

Node.js 24

This release updates the runtime to Node.js 24. v5 had preliminary support for Node.js 24, however this action was by default still running on Node.js 20. Now this action by default will run on Node.js 24.

What's Changed

  • Upload Artifact Node 24 support by @​salmanmkc in actions/upload-artifact#719
  • fix: update @​actions/artifact for Node.js 24 punycode deprecation by @​salmanmkc in actions/upload-artifact#744

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/compare/v5.0.0...v6.0.0

v5.0.0

What's Changed

BREAKING CHANGE: this update supports Node v24.x. This is not a breaking change per-se but we're treating it as such.

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v8.0.0): 🌈 Immutable releases and secure tags

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v7.6.0...v8.0.0)

##### This is the first immutable release of `setup-uv` 🥳

All future releases are also immutable, if you want to know more about what this means checkout [the docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases).

This release also has two breaking changes

##### New format for `manifest-file`

The previously deprecated way of defining a custom version manifest to control which `uv` versions are available and where to download them from got removed. The functionality is still there but you have to use the [new format](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/main/docs/customization.md#format).

##### No more major and minor tags

To increase **security** even more we will **stop publishing minor tags**. You won't be able to use `@v8` or `@v8.0` any longer. We do this because pinning to major releases opens up users to supply chain attacks like what happened to [tj-actions](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/).

> \[!TIP]
> Use the immutable tag as a version `astral-sh/setup-uv@v8.0.0`
> Or even better the githash `astral-sh/setup-uv@cec208311dfd045dd5311c1add060b2062131d57`

### [`v7.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v7.5.0): 🌈 Use `astral-sh/versions` as version provider

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v7.5.0...v7.5.0)

##### No more rate-limits

This release addresses a long-standing source of timeouts and rate-limit failures in setup-uv.

Previously, the action resolved version identifiers like 0.5.x by iterating over available uv releases via the GitHub API to find the best match. In contrast, latest and exact versions such as 0.5.0 skipped version resolution entirely and downloaded uv directly.

The `manifest-file` input was an earlier attempt to improve this. It allows providing an url to a file that lists available versions, checksums, and even custom download URLs. The action also shipped with such a manifest.
However, because that bundled file could become outdated whenever new uv releases were published, the action still had to fall back to the GitHub API in many cases.

This release solves the problem by sourcing version data from Astral’s versions repository via the raw content endpoint:

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/refs/heads/main/v1/uv.ndjson>

By using the raw endpoint instead of the GitHub API, version resolution no longer depends on API authentication and is much less likely to run into rate limits or timeouts.

***

> \[!TIP]
> The next section is only interesting for users of the `manifest-file` input

The `manifest-file` input lets you override that source with your own URL, for example to test custom uv builds or alternate download locations.

The manifest file must be in NDJSON format, where each line is a JSON object representing a version and its artifacts. For example:

```json
{"version":"0.10.7","artifacts":[{"platform":"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu","variant":"default","url":"https://example.com/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz","archive_format":"tar.gz","sha256":"..."}]}
{"version":"0.10.6","artifacts":[{"platform":"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu","variant":"default","url":"https://example.com/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz","archive_format":"tar.gz","sha256":"..."}]}
```

> \[!WARNING]\
> The old format still works but is deprecated. A warning will be logged when you use it.

##### Changes

[#​612](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/pull/612) fixed a faulty behavior where this action set `UV_CACHE_DIR` even though `enable-cache` was `false`. It also fixed the cases were the cache dir is already configured in a settings file like `pyproject.toml` or `UV_CACHE_DIR` was already set.  Here the action shouldn't overwrite or set `UV_CACHE_DIR`.

These fixes introduced an unwanted behavior: You can still set `cache-local-path` but this action didn't do anything. This release fixes that.

You can now use `cache-local-path` to automatically set `UV_CACHE_DIR` even when `enable-cache` is `false` (or gets set to false by default e.g. on self-hosted runners)

```yaml
- name: This is now possible
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
  with:
    enable-cache: false
    cache-local-path: "/path/to/cache"
```

**Support all the use cases!!!**

This release adds support for some use cases that most users don't encounter but are useful for e.g. people running Gitea.

This PR contains the following updates:

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>actions/github-script (actions/github-script)</summary>

### [`v9.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/releases/tag/v9.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/compare/v9.0.0...v9.0.0)

**New features:**

- **`getOctokit` factory function** — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See [Creating additional clients with `getOctokit`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script#creating-additional-clients-with-getoctokit) for details and examples.
- **Orchestration ID in user-agent** — The `ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID` environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

**Breaking changes:**

- **`require('@​actions/github')` no longer works in scripts.** The upgrade to `@actions/github` v9 (ESM-only) means `require('@​actions/github')` will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like `const { getOctokit } = require('@​actions/github')` to create secondary clients, use the new injected `getOctokit` function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
- `getOctokit` is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare `const getOctokit = ...` or `let getOctokit = ...` will get a `SyntaxError` because JavaScript does not allow `const`/`let` redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected `getOctokit` directly, or use `var getOctokit = ...` if you need to redeclare it.
- If your script accesses other `@actions/github` internals beyond the standard `github`/`octokit` client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

##### What's Changed

- Add ACTIONS\_ORCHESTRATION\_ID to user-agent string by [@​Copilot](https://redirect.github.com/Copilot) in [#​695](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/pull/695)
- ci: use deployment: false for integration test environments by [@​salmanmkc](https://redirect.github.com/salmanmkc) in [#​712](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/pull/712)
- feat!: add getOctokit to script context, upgrade [@​actions/github](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github) v9, [@​octokit/core](https://redirect.github.com/octokit/core) v7, and related packages by [@​salmanmkc](https://redirect.github.com/salmanmkc) in [#​700](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/pull/700)

##### New Contributors

- [@​Copilot](https://redirect.github.com/Copilot) made their first contribution in [#​695](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/pull/695)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/actions/github-script/compare/v8.0.0...v9.0.0>

### Release Notes

<details>

### [`v8.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v8.1.0): 🌈 New input `no-project`

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v8.0.0...v8.1.0)

#### Changes

This add the a new boolean input `no-project`.
It only makes sense to use in combination with `activate-environment: true` and will append `--no project` to the `uv venv` call. This is for example useful [if you have a pyproject.toml file with parts unparseable by uv](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/854)

#### 🚀 Enhancements

#### ⬆️ Dependency updates

- chore(deps): bump release-drafter/release-drafter from 7.1.1 to 7.2.0 @​[dependabot\[bot\]](https://redirect.github.com/apps/dependabot) ([#​855](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/855))

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v8.0.0): 🌈 Immutable releases and secure tags

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v7.6.0...v8.0.0)

##### This is the first immutable release of `setup-uv` 🥳

All future releases are also immutable, if you want to know more about what this means checkout [the docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases).

This release also has two breaking changes

##### New format for `manifest-file`

The previously deprecated way of defining a custom version manifest to control which `uv` versions are available and where to download them from got removed. The functionality is still there but you have to use the [new format](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/main/docs/customization.md#format).

##### No more major and minor tags

To increase **security** even more we will **stop publishing minor tags**. You won't be able to use `@v8` or `@v8.0` any longer. We do this because pinning to major releases opens up users to supply chain attacks like what happened to [tj-actions](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/).

### [`v7.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v7.5.0): 🌈 Use `astral-sh/versions` as version provider

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v7.5.0...v7.5.0)

##### No more rate-limits

This release addresses a long-standing source of timeouts and rate-limit failures in setup-uv.

Previously, the action resolved version identifiers like 0.5.x by iterating over available uv releases via the GitHub API to find the best match. In contrast, latest and exact versions such as 0.5.0 skipped version resolution entirely and downloaded uv directly.

The `manifest-file` input was an earlier attempt to improve this. It allows providing an url to a file that lists available versions, checksums, and even custom download URLs. The action also shipped with such a manifest.
However, because that bundled file could become outdated whenever new uv releases were published, the action still had to fall back to the GitHub API in many cases.

This release solves the problem by sourcing version data from Astral’s versions repository via the raw content endpoint:

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/refs/heads/main/v1/uv.ndjson>

By using the raw endpoint instead of the GitHub API, version resolution no longer depends on API authentication and is much less likely to run into rate limits or timeouts.

***

> \[!TIP]
> The next section is only interesting for users of the `manifest-file` input

The `manifest-file` input lets you override that source with your own URL, for example to test custom uv builds or alternate download locations.

The manifest file must be in NDJSON format, where each line is a JSON object representing a version and its artifacts. For example:

```json
{"version":"0.10.7","artifacts":[{"platform":"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu","variant":"default","url":"https://example.com/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz","archive_format":"tar.gz","sha256":"..."}]}
{"version":"0.10.6","artifacts":[{"platform":"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu","variant":"default","url":"https://example.com/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz","archive_format":"tar.gz","sha256":"..."}]}
```

> \[!WARNING]\
> The old format still works but is deprecated. A warning will be logged when you use it.

##### Changes

[#​612](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/pull/612) fixed a faulty behavior where this action set `UV_CACHE_DIR` even though `enable-cache` was `false`. It also fixed the cases were the cache dir is already configured in a settings file like `pyproject.toml` or `UV_CACHE_DIR` was already set.  Here the action shouldn't overwrite or set `UV_CACHE_DIR`.

These fixes introduced an unwanted behavior: You can still set `cache-local-path` but this action didn't do anything. This release fixes that.

You can now use `cache-local-path` to automatically set `UV_CACHE_DIR` even when `enable-cache` is `false` (or gets set to false by default e.g. on self-hosted runners)

```yaml
- name: This is now possible
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
  with:
    enable-cache: false
    cache-local-path: "/path/to/cache"
```

#### Changes

**Support all the use cases!!!**
... well, that we know of.

This release adds support for some use cases that most users don't encounter but are useful for e.g. people running Gitea.

The input `resolution-strategy` lets you use the lowest possible version of uv from a version range. Useful if you want to test your tool with different versions of uv.

### Release Notes

<summary>astral-sh/setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)</summary>

### [`v8.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v8.2.0): 🌈 New inputs `quiet` and `download-from-astral-mirror`

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v8.1.0...v8.2.0)

##### Changes

This release brings two new inputs and a few bug fixes.

##### New inputs

Lets talk about the new inputs first.

##### quiet

Pretty simple. It turns of all `info` loggings. Useful if you use this in a composite action and are not interested in all the details.
In the upcoming releases we will add log groups to fully implement support for "less noise"

> \[!NOTE]\
> Warnings and errors are always logged.

##### download-from-astral-mirror

In some cases you may want to directly use the fallback of checking for available versions and downloading releases from GitHub instead of using the astral.sh mirror. Setting `download-from-astral-mirror: false` allows you to do that.

##### Bugfixes

When using the astral.sh mirror to query available versions and download releases (done by default) we now stop sending the GitHub token in the header. The mirror never looked at it but we shouldn't be handing out that data even if it is just a short lived token.
All other bugfixes try to limit the impact of failed GitHub queries due to retries and other faults.

We couldn't pinpoint all rootcauses yet but added more logging for error cases to track them down.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [astral-sh/setup-uv](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv) | action | major | `v8.3.2` → `v9.0.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)</summary>

### [`v9.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v9.0.0): 🌈 Change `prune-cache` default to `false`

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v8.3.2...v9.0.0)

##### Changes

This release disables the default cache cache pruning to ease the load on the PyPi infrastructure.
Since users might experience more GitHub Actions cache usage which might result in higher costs this is marked as a breaking change. To read more on why we did this (now) you can read the detailed analysis and reasoning in [#​967](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/967)

Besides this big breaking change we also have a small bugfix while building caches for linux distributions that behave a big different than the "big ones" and a speed up in version resolution by only reading the version manifest until a matching version is found saving runtime and network bandwith.

##### 🚨 Breaking changes

- Change `prune-cache` default to `false` [@​charliermarsh](https://redirect.github.com/charliermarsh) ([#​967](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/967))

##### 🐛 Bug fixes

- fix: fall back to distribution ID when os-release has no version field [@​cxzhong](https://redirect.github.com/cxzhong) ([#​961](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/961))

##### 🚀 Enhancements

- Speed up version client by partial response reads [@​eifinger](https://redirect.github.com/eifinger) ([#​807](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/807))

##### 🧰 Maintenance

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/setup-uv (astral-sh/setup-uv)</summary>

### [`v10.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v10.0.0): 🌈 Disable automatic caching for sensitive events and new QOL features

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v9.0.0...v10.0.0)

##### Changes

Another breaking release, directly after v9.0.0 but we think the added security justifies that.

##### Extra security by default

If you use the default `enable-cache: auto` this will now **DISABLE THE CACHE** to protect against cache poisoning for the following events:

- `pull_request_target`
- `workflow_run`
- `release`

You can read the full reasoning in [#​984](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/issues/984)

##### `version: latest-known`

```yaml
- name: Install the latest version of uv known to setup-uv
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.0
  with:
    version: "latest-known"
```

This will now install the latest version with a checksum that is known by this action. The [known `uv` checksums](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/4f6036f71cec78afb113b323f220c9185d983c12/src/download/checksum/known-checksums.ts) are automatically updated but will take a release of this action to take effect. You won't be always using the latest & greatest but you will have an extra level of security.

##### Read python version from `.tool-versions`

```yaml
- name: Install uv based on the version defined in .tool-versions and also set python
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.0
  with:
    version-file: "pyproject.toml"
```

Will now also set the python version if it is defined in `.tool-versions`. You can read the details [in the docs](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/blob/main/docs/advanced-version-configuration.md#install-a-version-defined-in-a-requirements-or-config-file)

#### What's Changed

This release has a focus on increasing performance and reducing memory usage both on the client and server - but some fantastic new functionality crept in too, of course.

##### Highlights

- Open two views in side-by-side split view from any menu or `cmd`+`click` in [#​13044](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13044)
- Users with read-only access can now leave inline comments in [#​13209](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13209)
- Added `[[` trigger for mentioning or creating a document in [#​13402](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13402)
- Documents can now be shown with numbered headings, as a display preference in [#​13522](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13522)
- Sidebar sections can now be reordered by dragging their headers in [#​13505](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13505)
- Live document stats can now be displayed in the corner of the editor in [#​13318](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13318)
- Danish and Indonesian have been added to the available language options in [#​13221](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13221)
- Color swatches now have a hover card in the editor in [#​13192](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13192)
- Web pages, Email (`.eml`), TextPack, and PDF files can now be imported in [#​13229](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13229) [#​13235](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13235) [#​13302](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13302)

##### MCP

- Public share urls are now returned for documents in [#​13043](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13043)
- Available icon names are now exposed as a resource in [#​13048](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13048)
- All MCP tools now input and output Markdown consistently in [#​13234](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13234)
- Success payloads from MCP mutation tools now use less tokens in [#​13257](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13257)
- Archived documents are now excluded from MCP search by default in [#​13518](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13518)

##### Performance improvements

- The sidebar menu and navigation tree are faster by [@​Ali-ovo](https://redirect.github.com/Ali-ovo) in [#​12873](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/12873)
- Server memory usage is reduced, with container memory best practices documented in [#​13042](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13042)
- Boot migration check now runs as a separate process to reduce memory usage in [#​13049](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13049)
- Drag and drop re-rendering has been optimized in [#​13114](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13114)
- Local content search through the command menu is much faster and more accurate in [#​13115](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13115)
- Nested policies are now briefly cached on the server in [#​13172](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13172)
- Markdown import merge now uses an O(1) title lookup by [@​irontaek](https://redirect.github.com/irontaek) in [#​13117](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13117)
- The `revisions.list` endpoint now loads less data in [#​13202](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13202)
- `findByPk` now requires fewer database connections in [#​13214](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13214)
- Route chunks are now preloaded on sidebar hover intent in [#​13263](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13263)
- Search no longer needs to join on memberships in [#​13269](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13269)
- Search queries are now faster in [#​13293](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13293)
- The popularity score scan is now index-friendly and spread over an hour in [#​13306](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13306)
- Relationships are no longer fetched for newly created documents in [#​13308](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13308)
- Creating a new document is faster in [#​13310](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13310)
- Collection structure locks now use `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` in [#​13314](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13314)
- The document row lock is now taken after text processing in [#​13315](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13315)
- Deleting a document subtree no longer triggers N+1 queries in [#​13311](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13311)
- Mermaid is no longer part of the initial bundle in [#​13380](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13380)
- Browser tracing now sends fewer spans to Sentry in [#​13389](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13389)
- Revision diffs are now skipped when they are too expensive to compute in [#​13432](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13432)
- FontAwesome icon packs are no longer eagerly loaded in [#​13463](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13463)
- Loading of `y-prosemirror` has been reworked in [#​13521](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13521)
- The PWA precache is now limited and the service worker is skipped on share views in [#​13519](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13519)

##### Other improvements

- Small images are now inlined as base64 into exported HTML in [#​13036](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13036)
- A cleanup job now trims `search_queries` to match event log retention in [#​13035](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13035)
- Backlinks and References now have a context menu in [#​13045](https://redirect.github.com/outline/outline/pull/13045)

Note that with this release the ability to collapse any heading was removed. title: feat(rocketchat-oidc): add a verify hook that asks the chat server and the Jitsi web server
body:
The hook runs in the rocketchat service with the image's node: GET /api/info
must answer 200 with a version, and the bundled Jitsi web server must answer 200.

title: feat(coturn): verify asks turnserver for a TURN allocation with the REST secret
body:
The hook runs the image's turnutils_uclient against the relay with the REST
secret and -n 0, so no data is sent and the peer (outside denied-peer-ip) is
only parsed; a refused allocation exits nonzero and fails the check. The
sockets read keeps the TLS listeners, and the certificate check is unchanged.

title: feat(mailserver): verify asks Postfix and Dovecot instead of reading listening sockets
body:
The hook reads Postfix's banner and its EHLO answer on port 25 and Dovecot's
greeting on port 993 (openssl s_client), and keeps the rspamd EICAR branch for
a provided virus scanner.

title: feat(nextcloud-s3-oidc): verify also asks Apache for status.php
body:
After occ status, the hook asks http://localhost/status.php, as the boot probe
does: the instance must be installed and out of maintenance mode. A
maintenance mode that a backup or an update holds still ends the check ok.

title: feat(actualbudget): verify asks the running server for its build
body: The node hook requests /info on 5006 and requires the sync-server build name; a server held stopped by the backup quiesce (a node process in state T) answers ok.

title: feat(chatwoot): verify asks Rails for /api
body: The hook runs ruby in the rails service: GET /api on 3000 (with X-Forwarded-Proto for FORCE_SSL) must name a version and report Redis and Postgres ok.

title: feat(docuseal): verify asks the Rails server for /up and its manifest
body: The hook runs ruby in the docuseal service: /up answers 200 and /manifest names DocuSeal (X-Forwarded-Proto set for FORCE_SSL).

title: feat(easyappointments): verify asks Apache for the booking page
body: The hook requests http://localhost/ with the curl the healthcheck already uses and requires the Easy!Appointments page.

title: feat(element): verify asks Synapse for health and Matrix versions
body: The python hook runs in the synapse service: /health answers, /_matrix/client/versions lists a version, and with the call relay provided homeserver.yaml names it.

title: feat(espocrm): verify asks Apache for the start page and the REST API
body: The php hook runs as www-data in the espocrm service: / answers with the EspoCRM page and /api/v1/App/user answers 401.

title: feat(immich): verify asks the server to ping and name its version
body: The node hook requests /api/server/ping and /api/server/version on 2283 from the immich-server service.

title: feat(invoiceninja): verify asks the PHP application through nginx
body: The hook runs in the nginx service and requests /health with busybox wget; nginx hands it to php-fpm, so the PHP application must answer with its health reply.

title: feat(kimai): verify asks Apache for the sign-in page
body: The hook requests http://127.0.0.1:8001/login with curl (the image healthcheck's client) and requires the Kimai page.

title: feat(mautic): verify asks Apache for the sign-in page
body: The hook requests http://127.0.0.1/s/login with curl (the image healthcheck client), requires the Mautic page, and accepts the installer redirect of a site not yet installed.

title: feat(n8n): verify asks the server for its readiness
body: The hook requests /healthz/readiness on 5678 with node, which answers 200 once the database is connected and migrated.

title: feat(onlyoffice): verify asks the document server for /healthcheck
body: The hook requests http://127.0.0.1/healthcheck with curl (installed by the image, used by its healthcheck) and requires true.

title: feat(outline): verify asks the server for its sign-in configuration
body: The hook posts to /api/auth.config on 3000 with node, a public call that reads the database, with X-Forwarded-Proto set for FORCE_HTTPS.

title: feat(plane): verify asks the API and the object store
body: The hook asks /api/instances/ on the api service with python3 and, with USE_MINIO and AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL set, the store health endpoint.

title: feat(postiz): verify asks the backend and the front end
body: The hook requests /api/ (the backend root) and / through the bundled nginx on 5000 with node.

title: feat(twenty): verify asks the server for /healthz
body: The hook makes the request of the upstream compose healthcheck with curl and requires status ok.

title: feat(wordpress): verify asks nginx for the front page
body: The hook requests the front page from the wp service through nginx with php and looks for what WordPress sets.

title: feat(zammad): verify asks nginx for the sign-in state
body: The hook requests /api/v1/signshow on the nginx service with curl (installed by the image), a public call that nginx hands to Rails.

title: feat/import entry licence
body:
- **feat(import): read chosen entries and admit copyleft upstream projects**
- **feat(import): a copied compose file's licence is recorded, never a condition**

title: fix(ci): app-ci's image scan honours the accepted findings
body:
app-ci's image scan now reads `.scanctl/baseline.sarif`, as security.yml's reusable workflow does.

The app job ran `scanctl run` without `-baseline`, so a finding accepted in the baseline still failed it. An app whose compose file already exists at the base hides this, because the base scan already holds the same findings. A new app has no compose file at the base, so every finding of its images counted as added, the accepted ones included: the Umami pull request (#218) failed on the accepted `postgres:18.6-alpine` findings.

title: test(espocrm): assert the admin's customizations and the job runner i…
body:
…n test.yml

Seeds make the custom field cBenchNote on Account with a row in its detail layout through the admin API, leaving a field or row that is there as it is, and write custom/catena-bench-marker naming the run. Asserts read the field and the layout back through the API, the two files EspoCRM keeps them in and the marker through the container, and wait for a scheduled job whose last run is after the step began, so the job runner runs jobs in every leg.

title: test(rocketchat-oidc): a writer posts through the backup and its mess…
body:
…ages come back

The writer posts writer-<run>-<n> to the channel catena-<run> every 7 s as the first administrator, printing ack <n> for each post the server answered with success, and signs in again when its token is refused, while the backup holds the database. Its after step posts the record {{ writer_id }} once the backup is over. After the restore the check lists the channel's messages and finds every acknowledged post and not the record. The login is read from the container's environment.

title: test(wordpress): assert the converge curation and the mail wiring in test.yml
body:
The block declares the hosts the configure hook reaches (wp-cli on GitHub,
the WordPress.org plugin API and downloads) as its egress. Asserts require
the curated plugins active, the Redis object cache on and connected, the
cache options seeded once, and WP Mail SMTP's relay host, port, user, sender
and encryption equal to the relay the host holds; the relay password is the
WPMS_SMTP_PASS constant, compared by sha256, and the option holds none. A
seed makes an administrator's edits to a cache option and the sender name,
and the asserts hold them after every deploy of the legs.

title: test(actualbudget): a writer uploads through the backup and its files come back
body:
The writer uploads one file after another through the sync server's API in
its container, printing ack <n> for each upload the server answers ok, while
the backup stops and continues the server. Its after step uploads the record
{{ writer_id }} once the backup is over. After the restore the check runs
SQLite's integrity check on copies of the server's .sqlite files, downloads
every file acknowledged before the backup with the bytes sent, and finds the
record gone. The test password is read from the environment.

title: build: run the catalog tools in one locked uv project
body:
## Cause

The repo had no pyproject.toml and no uv.lock. Each `build/*.py` carried a PEP 723 `# /// script` block, so every `uv run build/x.py` built its own unlocked environment from ranges. The tests ran as `uv run --with pytest --with jsonschema --with pyyaml --with pillow --with resvg-py pytest` (Makefile, build-and-verify.yml:226), also unlocked. `images/erpnext-helpdesk/build.py` ran on a bare python3.

## Change

- New root `pyproject.toml`: jsonschema, pillow, pyyaml and resvg-py, with pytest in a dev group. No build system and no `[tool.uv]`, because app-dispatch sets UV_NO_CONFIG. Plus `uv.lock`.
- The 11 inline blocks are removed. The `uv run` shebangs stay. `uv help run`: "When running a script, the project or workspace is discovered from the script's directory". So `uv run "$TOOLS/build/x.py"` from a workflow_call caller's tree uses this lock. This was tested from a cwd that holds another project.
- Makefile: `make test` runs `uv run --locked pytest tests/ images/erpnext-helpdesk -q`, and serve runs `uv run python -m http.server`.
- `build/render-ci.sh` now runs `exec uv run --locked build/render.py`. The python3 fallback and the optional jsonschema behind it (`lib/model.py`, two tests in `tests/test_model.py`, the guard import in `build/validate.py`) are removed. Its one caller, ops `automation/operator-tools/bump_versions.py:594,754`, runs in catena-admin engine-bump.yml after setup-uv (`:103`).
- `images/erpnext-helpdesk`: build.py gets the uv shebang, and the README and test_build.py docstring use `uv run`.
- `renovate.json`: the pep723 rule becomes pep621. The shared preset already relocks uv locks. scanctl already scans any uv.lock (scanctl `internal/detect/detect.go:59-70`), so the security config needs no change.
- `tests/test_uv_project.py` checks three things: no tracked `.py` file has a script block, the Makefile has no `--with`, and every `--with` package in a workflow is a project dependency. uv then reports "Base environment satisfies requirements" and installs nothing outside the lock.

- `uv run --locked pytest tests/ images/erpnext-helpdesk`: 1945 passed, 10 skipped.
- `build/validate.py`: OK. `build/render.py` and `bash build/render-ci.sh`: no drift in blueprints, catalog.json or index.html.
- lint_quiesce, lint_postgres_pins and lint_swarm: pass.
- check-prose and check-unicode: clean.
- `uv lock --check` with uv 0.11.27: passes.

Note: uv 0.11.27 does not find the project from the script's directory, but 0.13.6 does. Every workflow step that runs `uv run "$TOOLS/build/..."` installs the latest uv through setup-uv first.

title: docs(coturn): say where Nextcloud Talk lists the relay
body:
## Cause

Ops issue 473: the relay's tile read "Not reachable" with a grey dot, and nothing said whether Nextcloud Talk uses the relay. coturn's declaration is correct. An app with no web address has no `vps.route.host` (AGENTS.md), and the panel fix is in catena-admin (`fix(apps): show an app with no web address as a background app` and `feat(apps): give the tile of an app with no web address its last verify`). The Nextcloud configure hook already writes Talk's STUN and TURN entries (`blueprints/nextcloud/hooks/configure.sh` `wire_turn`).

## Change

- `blueprints/coturn/app.json`: step 3 of the EN and FR setup steps says that the Talk page of Nextcloud's administration settings lists the relay among its STUN and TURN servers. The Nextcloud Talk docs (TURN page) name "Nextcloud admin panel > Talk settings", with "STUN servers" and "TURN server".
- `catalog.json`: the render's output.
- No block field changes, and `requires_catena` stays.

A Nextcloud verify check of Talk's relay entries was considered and dropped. A failing verify rolls an update back (catena-admin `payload/engines/stackupdate/folders.go` `verifyUpdate`), so a person who removed the relay from Talk would block every Nextcloud update.

## What ran

- `make render`: only `catalog.json` moved.
- `make lint`: OK.
- `make test`: 1945 passed, 10 skipped.
- `check-prose` and `check-unicode`: clean.

The branch also holds `.agent/plan.md` and `.agent/checkpoint.md`, to be removed before the merge.

title: fix(umami): open the heartbeat path to the status check
body:
The status page probes https://<address>/api/heartbeat without signing in and expects 200 with ok. On Umami's admin-only address only the tracker script and the collect path were public, so the sign-in gate answered 302 and Umami showed red while it ran.

/api/heartbeat joins vps.auth.public_paths (3 of the 8 allowed). It answers {"ok":true} and nothing else.

title: docs: a merged fork pull request carries the verdict of adopt/<pr> (GH#293)
body:
Ref #293

The behaviour lives in `.github/workflows/app-dispatch.yml`, which this token cannot push. This PR carries the README line; the workflow diff below is for a maintainer to apply. README describes the behaviour once the diff lands.

## Workflow diff (apply to `.github/workflows/app-dispatch.yml`)

```diff
@@ -253,6 +253,16 @@ jobs:
               '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == env.DEFAULT_BRANCH)]
                | .[0].head.sha // empty' || true
           }
+          # The head of branch adopt/<pr>, <pr> being the pull request merged as commit $1.
+          adopt_head() {
+            local pr
+            pr="$(gh api "repos/$OWNER/$REPO_NAME/commits/$1/pulls" 2>/dev/null --jq \
+              '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == env.DEFAULT_BRANCH)]
+               | .[0].number // empty' || true)"
+            [[ "$pr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
+            gh api "repos/$OWNER/$REPO_NAME/git/ref/heads/adopt/$pr" 2>/dev/null \
+              --jq '.object.sha' || true
+          }
           : > "$RUNNER_TEMP/payloads.txt"
           while read -r sha base ids <&3; do
             carry_state=""
@@ -276,6 +286,11 @@ jobs:
                   prev=""
                 fi
                 if [ -n "$prev" ] && qualifies "$prev" "$ids"; then taken="$prev"; fi
+                # A fork's head carries no status here: its change was tested on adopt/<pr>.
+                if [ -z "$taken" ] && [ "$BRANCH" = "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
+                  prev="$(adopt_head "$sha")"
+                  if [ -n "$prev" ] && qualifies "$prev" "$ids"; then taken="$prev"; fi
+                fi
               fi
               if [ -z "$taken" ]; then
                 tag_run="$(uv run "$TOOLS/build/versions.py" tested-run "$ids" --ref "$sha" || true)"
```

`qualifies` already requires the CI App as creator, an ops run address, a description naming exactly the app, and `versions.py same` (presentation-only difference), so the adopt head is carried only when the app's files match.

none

title: GH#332: fix(mailserver): wait for Dovecot mailbox readiness
body:
## Summary

Wait for Dovecot's user lookup before the mailserver users hook reports success. The account source file is updated by `setup email add`, but the image's watcher populates Dovecot's userdb asynchronously. Check every desired mailbox, including an unchanged account on a rerun. Share one 120-second deadline, bound each lookup, and keep the ownership record when readiness fails.

Resolves #332

## Cause and evidence

[Original app-tests lifecycle log](https://github.com/catenahq/ops/actions/runs/43707383301/job/132791846634):
- At 11:39:20 Roundcube reports `IMAP Error: Login failed` on `AUTHENTICATE OAUTHBEARER` and the OAuth callback returns 401.
- Dovecot reports `user not found from any userdbs`, `Authenticated user not found from userdb`, and `1/1 successful auths` for the same attempt.
- Dovecot reloads at 11:39:21.

The hook's old completion condition covered the source account list, not Dovecot's readiness. No OAuth callback retry, authentication setting, password, mailbox ownership or removal rule is changed.

## Files changed

- `blueprints/mailserver/hooks/users.py`: bounded live userdb readiness check.
- `blueprints/mailserver/docker-compose.yml`: generated packed hook.

title: GH#334: blocked checkpoint for Collabora WOPI host restriction
body:
For #334

## Blocked checkpoint - do not merge

The managed host and documented alias-group wiring are implemented, but exact-host security acceptance is unresolved. This draft is a recovery checkpoint, not a completed security fix. The issue must remain open.

## Summary

- Replace `domain` with `aliasgroup1` driven by managed `WOPI_HOST`, following Nextcloud's zone-derived hostname.
- Require a nonempty managed value at compose interpolation.
- Preserve the image, routing, TLS termination, iframe access and existing health probe.
- Render the compose and catalog through the existing build tools.

## Blocking evidence

The public Collabora co-25.04 `wsd/HostUtil.cpp` passes a canonical group's `Poco::URI::getHost()` into the WOPI regex allowlist. Its `common/RegexUtil.cpp` falls back to regex matching, so dots in a plain hostname can admit lookalikes. Independent review also found that public Poco's URI host parser lowercases the canonical host, so a proposed PCRE `\Q...\E` quotation can become `\q...\e`. That quotation has been removed from the current head.

These public-source findings identify a concrete risk, not a reproduced result on `26.04.6.1.1`. Required pinned-runtime positive and explicit-negative evidence is still absent. A health-only app-tests pass cannot resolve it.

The current catena-admin `payload/engines/appenv/expr.go` parser accepts bare values, defaults, md5 hashing and lowercasing, but not replacement or regex-escape filters. A template cannot safely invent such a filter. A supported exact-host configuration on the pinned image would avoid a prerequisite; otherwise the minimal proposed prerequisite is a tested regex-escape expression capability in catena-admin, published before this catalog raises `requires_catena` to use it. That repository and release are outside this worker's authorized scope.

## Verification

- Validation, hook lint, Postgres pin lint, and static swarm lint pass.
- Initial scoped catalog/model/pack/render/app-test declaration suite: 472 passed, 1 skipped. The current head additionally passes render, validation, hook lint and whitespace checks.
- Second-render hashes were identical before the final configuration-only correction.
- Unicode gate passes (376 files).
- Prose gate cannot run with the installed Vale version: contracts pins 3.21.0, but the runner has 3.27.0. No prose gate configuration or debt file is changed.
- Docker's stack loader is unavailable locally and remains a CI check.

## Runtime Testing

Not verified. No container is launched and no image is pulled, as required by the worker runbook. The separate app-test PR must prove allowed-host authorization and explicit denial of foreign and dot-substitution hosts, before and after an allowed request. Network failures are not denial evidence.

## Reserved files

None.

## Scenarios checked

- `blueprints/collabora/test.yml`: unchanged; it runs the server's health probe. Its security regression must be a separate PR under repository policy.
- Nextcloud's host expression: read-only; the new key uses its existing address convention.
- No cross-repository bench or consumer modification is claimed or performed.

## Bench to prove it

The Collabora app-tests lifecycle plus pinned-image host-authorization regression. Neither the exact-host requirement nor the full issue is complete.

## Findings

The blocked exact-host transformation and proposed catena-admin prerequisite remain tracked on issue #334. No other repository or workflow is modified.
